fix_summary.problem: TOCTOU race condition in _ensure_parent_directory - validation and mkdir not atomic
fix_summary.root_cause: Time-of-check to time-of-use gap between exists() check and mkdir() with exist_ok=False
fix_summary.solution: Use exist_ok=True in mkdir() to handle concurrent directory creation gracefully

security_analysis.attack_vector: An attacker could create a file/directory at the parent path between the exists() check and mkdir() call, causing FileExistsError or potential symlink attacks
security_analysis.mitigation: Using exist_ok=True eliminates the race window by making mkdir() idempotent - if the directory already exists (created by another process), it succeeds instead of failing

test_scenarios: Concurrent directory creation with multiple processes
Verification that exist_ok=True is used in mkdir
Race condition simulation between exists() and mkdir()
Full save() flow with concurrent directory creation
Verification that file-as-directory validation still works

risks_and_limitations.backward_compatibility: No breaking changes - the fix only makes mkdir more resilient
risks_and_limitations.edge_cases: The file-as-directory validation (lines 35-40) still has a minor TOCTOU gap, but this is acceptable because: (1) the mkdir with exist_ok=True handles concurrent creation, (2) if an attacker replaces a directory with a file, the operation will fail safely with an error
risks_and_limitations.performance_impact: None - same number of operations, just different parameter
